headline: Showers end tonight; dry, sunny, frosty mornings through Monday, then a chance of midweek rain.
summary: A slow low pressure system is leaving to the southeast, and high pressure is building in behind it. That brings dry, sunny weather into early next week, with cold air from the northeast letting nights drop to the 30s. Frost is likely in the southern foothills and valleys and south of the Olympics, spreading more widely by Monday. Clouds return Tuesday as a weak atmospheric river, a stream of moisture, mostly aims at British Columbia. Rain could reach western Washington midweek, but forecasters are unsure, and many computer model runs keep us dry. Warmer, drier weather should arrive Thursday, with highs in the low 70s by Friday. Rain and cooler air could return by the weekend.
